feedback.correct: You found it! It goes plop into the pot — Tara claps for you!
feedback.retry: No rush at all — Tara says the word again, slow and soft. Listen, then tap.

hint_sequence: Tara says the question again, slowly and softly.
Tara points: look at each picture, one by one.
Tara starts the word for you — 'po… po…' Which one goes po-TA-to?

interactions.prompt: Tara needs the potato for the curry. Which one is the potato?
Tara asks: which one is long and orange — the carrot?
Nani wants something sweet — a FRUIT. Which one of these is a fruit?

objective: Name and recognize six common fruit-and-vegetable words: tomato, potato, onion, pea, carrot, banana.
off_screen: Pack a real kitchen basket together and name every fruit and vegetable that goes inside.
parent_note: Words: naming and recognizing six kitchen words — tomato, potato, onion, pea, carrot, banana — each demonstrated in a little sentence scene.

story_beats.art_note: Warm Indian kitchen; Tara holds up a round red tomato, Nani smiles beside a pot.
story_beats.text: Tara is helping Nani cook lunch! 'First we need vegetables. Look — this one is round and red and shiny. Tomato! Say it with me: to-MA-to.'

story_beats.art_note: Tara rolling a brown potato; small thought-puff of soil and roots.
story_beats.text: Tara rolls a brown, round one across the table. 'This one is brown and round, and it grows under the ground. Potato! Po-TA-to.'

story_beats.art_note: Tara holding a sliced onion (layers visible), peas tumbling from a small bowl.
story_beats.text: 'Achoo!' Tara sniffles and giggles. 'This one has round layers and makes our eyes water. Onion! O-ni-on. And these tiny green balls — peas! They roll!'
Nani calls from the stove: 'Lunch is almost ready!' Tara laughs: 'You learned my kitchen words! Now help me find them in the basket.'
Nani tastes the curry — 'Delicious!' Everyone claps. Tara twirls: 'You are a true kitchen-word star!'

subject: words
title: Tara's Kitchen Basket
